Released in North America on September 25, 2000, and in Europe on March 2, 2001, its Puzzle League-based gameplay has a focus on puzzle-based strategy in the game's grid-based format.
info.trivia: A Panel de Pon game dressed in the Pokémon anime, released only in the West.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than the other Pokémon N64 titles, so it prices above them.

info.about: Mario Party 3 is a 2000 party video game developed by Hudson Soft and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. The third installment in the Mario Party series, it was first released in Japan on December 7, 2000, in North America on May 7, 2001, in Australia on September 3, 2001, and in Europe on November 16, 2001.
info.trivia: It arrived in May 2001, after the GameCube had been announced.
info.why: A late release with a smaller run than the first two, and the most requested of the trio, so it is the most expensive.

info.about: Mario Party 2 is a 1999 party video game developed by Hudson Soft and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. The second game in the Mario Party series, it was released in Japan on December 17, 1999, North America on January 24, 2000, and in PAL regions on October 13, 2000.
info.trivia: Widely considered the best of the N64 trilogy and re-released on Switch Online.
info.why: Common; the re-release keeps demand for the cart moderate.

info.about: Castlevania: Legacy of Darkness is a 1999 action-adventure game developed and published by Konami for the Nintendo 64.
info.trivia: An expanded re-release of Castlevania 64 with new characters, published late in the console's life.
info.why: Printed in far smaller numbers than the original and never re-released, so it is the expensive one of the pair.

info.about: Turok 2: Seeds of Evil is a first-person shooter video game developed by Iguana Entertainment and published by Acclaim Entertainment. It was released for the Nintendo 64 console in 1998 and ported to Microsoft Windows computers in 1999.
info.trivia: One of the first games to support the Expansion Pak's high-resolution mode.
info.why: Very common, and a 2017 remaster covers players who just want to play, so prices are low.

info.about: Jet Force Gemini is a 1999 third-person shooter game developed and published by Rare for the Nintendo 64. The game follows the story of three members of a galactic law enforcement team as they try to stop a horde of drones led by an insectoid called Mizar.
info.trivia: The original release made you rescue every last scattered Tribal to reach the finale; later re-releases eased the requirement.
info.why: A late Rare cartridge with a modest print run, lifted by the collector interest in Rare's whole N64 catalogue.

info.about: Blast Corps is a 1997 action game developed by Rare and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. The player uses vehicles to destroy buildings in the path of a runaway nuclear missile carrier.
info.trivia: Rare's demolition puzzler was among the studio's first N64 games and was later included in Rare Replay.
info.why: Moderate supply and a re-release keep it mid-priced.

info.about: Wave Race 64 is a 1996 racing video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It is the second entry in the Wave Race series following the 1992 Game Boy game Wave Race.
info.trivia: A launch-window title whose water physics were a showpiece for the hardware.
info.why: Very common; prices are driven by condition.

info.about: 1080° Snowboarding is a snowboarding video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64 in 1998.
info.trivia: Made in-house at Nintendo EAD and re-released on Virtual Console.
info.why: Common and re-released, so prices stay low.

info.about: Excitebike 64 is a 2000 racing video game developed by Left Field Productions and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It is the second installment in the Excite series, acting as a sequel to the 1984 NES game Excitebike, and is the first 3D game in the series.
info.trivia: Left Field's motocross game shipped with the original NES Excitebike as an unlockable.
info.why: A moderate print run and a Wii U Virtual Console release keep it mid-priced.

info.about: Hybrid Heaven is a 1999 action role playing game developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Osaka and published by Konami for Nintendo 64. This game is most notable for its peculiar mix of genres: it has aspects of both role-playing video games and action-adventure games.
info.trivia: Konami's odd mix of adventure and turn-based wrestling combat, one of few N64 RPGs.
info.why: A small print run and the scarcity of role-playing games on the system give it cult demand.

info.about: Quest 64 is a role-playing video game (RPG) developed by Imagineer for the Nintendo 64. It was released in North America in June 1998 by THQ, Europe in September 1998 by Konami and Japan in July 1999 by Imagineer.
info.trivia: The first RPG released for the N64 in North America.
info.why: THQ printed plenty and it was poorly reviewed, so supply is fine; its status as one of the console's few RPGs keeps a floor under the price.

info.about: Doom 64 is a 1997 first-person shooter game developed and published by Midway Games for the Nintendo 64.
info.trivia: A new Doom rather than a port, with its own levels and a darker tone; remastered in 2020.
info.why: Common enough, and the remaster gives players an easy alternative, so the cart is mid-priced.

info.about: Resident Evil 2 is a 1998 survival horror game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation. The player controls rookie cop Leon S.
info.trivia: Angel Studios squeezed two CDs of game onto a 64 MB cartridge, the largest ever made for the system.
info.why: A technical curiosity with a smaller print run than the PlayStation version, and never re-released in this form.

info.about: Worms Armageddon is a 1999 turn-based strategy video game developed and published by Team17 as part of the Worms series. It was originally released for the Microsoft Windows operating system, and was later ported to the PlayStation, Dreamcast, Nintendo 64, and Game Boy Color.
info.trivia: A late Infogrames release, arriving in 2000 when few third parties were still publishing on the system.
info.why: A small print run and no other way to own this version make it one of the pricier third-party carts.

info.about: Pokémon Stadium 2, known in Japan as Pokémon Stadium Gold & Silver, is a strategy video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It is the third game in the Pokémon Stadium series, following prior releases Pocket Monsters Stadium and Pokémon Stadium.
Mario Party is a 1998 party video game developed by Hudson Soft and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. The game was targeted at a young audience.

Mario Tennis is a sports video game developed by Camelot Software Planning and published in 2000 by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. Following Mario's Tennis, it is the second game in the Mario Tennis series.

Mario Golf is a 1999 sports video game developed by Camelot Software Planning and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It is the successor to NES Open Tournament Golf and, although the first to bear the name, is the second game in the Mario Golf series.

Yoshi's Story is a 1997 platform game published and developed by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. Following the Super NES game Yoshi's Island (1995), it is the second main installment in the Yoshi series.

Diddy Kong Racing is a 1997 kart racing game developed and published by Rare for the Nintendo 64. The game revolves around Diddy Kong and his friends' attempt to defeat the intergalactic antagonist, a wizard pig named Wizpig, through winning a series of races.

Pilotwings 64 is a 1996 flight simulation video game developed by Nintendo and Paradigm Simulation and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It was one of three launch titles for the Nintendo 64 in Japan as well as Europe and one of two launch titles in North America, along with Super Mario 64.

games.title: Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire

info.about: Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire is a 1996 action video game developed by LucasArts and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It is primarily a third-person shooter, with multiple types of vehicular combat and third-person shooting sequences.

Star Wars: Rogue Squadron or Star Wars: Rogue Squadron 3D is an arcade-style flight action game co-developed by Factor 5 and LucasArts. The first of the Rogue Squadron trilogy, it was published by LucasArts and Nintendo and released for Microsoft Windows and Nintendo 64 in December 1998.
Star Wars Episode I: Racer is a 1999 racing video game developed and published by LucasArts. It is based on the podracing sequence in the film Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace.

games.title: Star Wars Episode I: Battle for Naboo

info.about: Star Wars Episode I: Battle for Naboo is an arcade-style action game co-developed by Factor 5 and LucasArts. It is a spiritual successor to Star Wars: Rogue Squadron released two years earlier.

Turok: Dinosaur Hunter is a first-person shooter video game developed by Iguana Entertainment and published by Acclaim Entertainment. It was released in 1997 in North America and Europe for the Nintendo 64 and Microsoft Windows, and is an adaptation of the comic book series of the same name from Valiant Comics.

Turok 3: Shadow of Oblivion is a 2000 first-person shooter video game developed by Acclaim Studios Austin and published by Acclaim Entertainment for the Nintendo 64. It is the third main installment of the Turok series, and a sequel to 1998's Turok 2: Seeds of Evil.
Killer Instinct Gold is a 1996 fighting game developed by Rare and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It is based on the arcade game Killer Instinct 2.

Mortal Kombat Trilogy is a 1996 fighting game released by Midway as the second and final update to Mortal Kombat 3 for the PlayStation, Nintendo 64, Sega Saturn and PCs. Further versions were also released for the Game.com and R-Zone.
Mortal Kombat 4 is a 1997 fighting game developed and published by Midway for arcades. It is the fourth main installment in the Mortal Kombat franchise, and a sequel to 1995's Mortal Kombat 3.

WCW/nWo Revenge is a professional wrestling video game developed by Asmik Ace Entertainment and AKI Corporation and released by THQ in 1998 for the Nintendo 64 game console. It is the sequel to 1997's WCW vs. nWo: World Tour.

WWF No Mercy is a professional wrestling video game released in 2000 by THQ for the Nintendo 64. It is based on the World Wrestling Federation and is named after the WWF's annual event of the same name.
WWF WrestleMania 2000 is a professional wrestling video game released in 1999 on the Nintendo 64 (N64) console. It was based on the World Wrestling Federation's annual pay-per-view, WrestleMania.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, released as Tony Hawk's Skateboarding in the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand, and parts of Europe, is a 1999 skateboarding video game developed by Neversoft and published by Activision. It is the first installment in the Tony Hawk's series.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 is a 2000 skateboarding video game developed by Neversoft for PlayStation and Natsume for Game Boy Color. Published by Activision, it is the second installment in the Tony Hawk's series of sports games, and was released for the PlayStation in 2000, with subsequent ports to Windows and Dreamcast alongside a distinct version for Game Boy Color the same year.
Rayman 2: The Great Escape is a 1999 platform game developed by Ubi Pictures and published by Ubi Soft for Windows, the Nintendo 64, Dreamcast and PlayStation.

Mega Man Legends is a 1997 action-adventure game released by Capcom. It is the first game in the Mega Man Legends sub-series of Mega Man games from Capcom, and the second major 3D polygonal Mega Man title in the franchise, following Mega Man: Battle & Chase.
Castlevania, also informally referred to as Castlevania 64, is a 1999 action-adventure game developed and published by Konami for the Nintendo 64.
Duke Nukem 3D is a 1996 first-person shooter game developed by 3D Realms and published by FormGen for MS-DOS.

Duke Nukem: Zero Hour is a 1999 third-person shooter game in the Duke Nukem series, developed by Eurocom and published by GT Interactive for the Nintendo 64. The game uses a relatively large 32 megabyte cartridge and can also use the Expansion Pak to improve graphics, though this slows down the frame rate.

Bomberman 64 is a video game developed and published by Hudson Soft as "Baku Bomberman" in Japan, and published by Nintendo as "Bomberman 64" in North America and Europe for the Nintendo 64. In Japan the "Bomberman 64" name was chosen for another game, the fourth Japanese N64 entry in the series.

Bomberman Hero is a platform video game developed by A.I Co., Ltd. and published by Hudson Soft for the Nintendo 64. It is the second Bomberman game to be released on the system, following Bomberman 64 (1997).
Snowboard Kids , is a snowboarding video game for the Nintendo 64. It was developed by Racdym and published by Atlus.

Aidyn Chronicles: The First Mage is a 2001 role-playing video game developed by Canadian studio H2O Entertainment and published by THQ for the Nintendo 64 video game console. It was released in North America on March 20, 2001, and in Europe on August 3, 2001.

Gauntlet Legends is a 1998 hack and slash video game developed and published by Atari Games for arcades. It is a sequel to 1985's Gauntlet and 1986's Gauntlet II, and the final game in the Gauntlet series to be produced by Atari Games.

Cruis'n USA is a racing video game developed by TV Games Inc. and published by Nintendo. It was first released in arcades in 1994 by Midway Games, with a port to the Nintendo 64 developed by Leland Interactive Media released in 1996.
Cruis'n World is a 1996 racing game developed by Midway Games and published by Nintendo. It is the sequel to the 1994 arcade racer Cruis'n USA.

San Francisco Rush: Extreme Racing is a 1996 racing video game developed and published by Atari Games for arcades. It was ported to home consoles under the Midway label, beginning with the Nintendo 64 in 1997 and the PlayStation and Windows in 1998.
Rush 2: Extreme Racing USA is a 1998 racing video game developed by Atari Games and published by Midway exclusively for the Nintendo 64.

San Francisco Rush 2049 is a 1999 racing video game developed and manufactured by Atari Games for arcades, later ported to home systems. It is the third game in the Rush series as the sequel to San Francisco Rush: Extreme Racing and Rush 2: Extreme Racing USA as well as the last to be set in the city of San Francisco.
Beetle Adventure Racing! is a racing game released for the Nintendo 64 in 1999. It was developed by Paradigm Entertainment and EA Canada, and published by Electronic Arts.

Hydro Thunder is an arcade inshore powerboat racing video game originally released by Midway Games in February 1999 and later released for the Sega Dreamcast as a launch title later that year. It was also released for the PlayStation and Nintendo 64 in early 2000.

NFL Blitz is an American football video game developed and published by Midway for the arcade in 1997, the first game in the NFL Blitz series. The development team was headed by Mark Turmell and Sal Divita, who were known for being behind NBA Jam, and NFL Blitz was a deliberate attempt to translate the exaggerated arcade-style approach of NBA Jam to the football realm.

Wipeout 64 is a 1998 racing video game developed by Psygnosis and published by Midway Games for the Nintendo 64. It is the third game in the Wipeout series and remains the only one published on a Nintendo console.

Extreme-G is a futuristic racing video game developed by Probe Entertainment and published by Acclaim Entertainment, featuring an original trance soundtrack. It was released for the Nintendo 64 in 1997, with a Japan release on May 29, 1998.
Glover is a 1998 puzzle-platformer developed by Interactive Studios and published by Hasbro Interactive for the Nintendo 64 and Windows in 1998, and for the PlayStation in 1999.
Chameleon Twist is a 1997 video game developed by Japan System Supply, published by Japan System Supply in Japan, and published by Sunsoft in North America and Europe for the Nintendo 64.

Tetrisphere is a puzzle video game developed by H2O Entertainment and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. It was released in North America on August 11, 1997, and in PAL regions in February 1998.

Dr. Mario 64 is a 2001 tile-matching action puzzle game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. The game is an enhanced remake of Dr. Mario, which was originally released for the NES and Game Boy consoles in 1990, and is based around characters from the 2000 Game Boy Color game Wario Land 3.

Hey You, Pikachu! is a virtual pet video game developed by Ambrella and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 64. A spin-off in the Pokémon franchise, it was released in Japan on December 12, 1998, and in North America on November 6, 2000.

Silent Hill 2 is a 2001 survival horror video game developed by Konami's Team Silent and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2. The second installment in the Silent Hill series, Silent Hill 2 centers on James Sunderland, a widower who journeys to the town of Silent Hill after receiving a letter from his dead wife.
info.trivia: Konami's in-house Team Silent built the fog and grain out of hardware limits, then kept them because they made the town feel wrong.
info.why: Never given a faithful re-release — the HD Collection was widely criticised — so the original disc stayed the best way to play it, and the 2024 remake sent a wave of new players looking for it.

annotation.note: The Bloober Team remake sent new players looking for the PS2 original, which has never been re-released digitally.

info.about: Silent Hill 3 is a 2003 survival horror video game developed by Konami's Team Silent and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2. The third installment in the Silent Hill series and a direct sequel to the first Silent Hill game follows Heather Mason, a teenager who becomes entangled in the machinations of the town's cult, which seeks to revive a malevolent deity.
info.trivia: A direct sequel to the first game, with a soundtrack that Akira Yamaoka considers his best work.
info.why: The 2012 HD Collection was poorly received, so players seeking the intended version buy the PS2 disc, and it was printed in smaller numbers than Silent Hill 2.

info.about: Silent Hill 4: The Room is a 2004 survival horror video game developed by Konami's Team Silent and published by Konami. The fourth installment in the Silent Hill series, the game was released in Japan in June and in North America and Europe in September.
info.trivia: It began as a separate project before being folded into the series, and is the only entry with a first-person apartment.
info.why: Common, and available on PC since 2020, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Rule of Rose is a 2006 survival horror video game developed by Punchline and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. Set in Britain in 1930, the plot revolves around a nineteen-year-old woman named Jennifer, who finds herself trapped in a world dominated by young girls who have formed a social hierarchy known as the Red Crayon Aristocrats.
info.trivia: European politicians campaigned against it on the strength of press reports that badly misdescribed its content, and it went unreleased in the UK.
info.why: A very small Atlus print run in North America, plus the notoriety of the European controversy, on a game that has never been reissued.

annotation.note: Low print run plus a persistent Atlus-adjacent collector following; sealed copies regularly clear four figures.

info.about: Haunting Ground is a 2005 survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. The story follows Fiona Belli, a young woman who wakes up in the dungeon of a castle after being involved in a car accident.
info.trivia: Released as Demento in Japan. Your dog Hewie is commanded with the shoulder buttons and genuinely can be trained, or neglected.
info.why: Capcom's last original PS2 survival horror, printed late in the generation and never re-released in any form.

info.about: Kuon is a 2004 survival horror video game developed by FromSoftware for the PlayStation 2. Published by FromSoftware in Japan, it was released in North America by Agetec, and in Europe by Nobilis and Indie Games Productions in 2006.
info.trivia: A Heian-period Japanese horror game made by FromSoftware a decade before Dark Souls made the studio a household name.
info.why: A tiny Agetec print run met a demand spike once FromSoftware became famous, and there has never been a reissue.

annotation.note: Elden Ring renewed interest in FromSoftware's back catalogue, and Kuon had a very small US print run.

info.about: Obscure is a survival horror video game developed by Hydravision Entertainment and published by DreamCatcher Interactive in North America, Ubisoft in China and MC2-Microïds in other territories for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 2 and Xbox.
info.trivia: A teen-horror co-op game from French studio Hydravision, published by DreamCatcher.
info.why: A small print run from a minor publisher; the PC and Xbox versions exist but the PS2 disc is the one collectors want.

info.about: Obscure II, known in North America as Obscure: The Aftermath, is a survival horror video game developed by Hydravision Entertainment and published by Playlogic in PAL regions and Ignition in North America for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 2 and Wii. It is the sequel to the 2004 video game Obscure.
info.trivia: The sequel came to PS2 in 2008 alongside Wii and PSP versions, late in the console's life.
info.why: The PS2 version was the smallest run of the three, so it prices above them.

info.about: God Hand is a 2006 beat 'em up game developed by Clover Studio and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. It was released in Japan and North America in 2006, and in 2007 for PAL territories.
info.trivia: Directed by Shinji Mikami and released weeks before Capcom dissolved Clover Studio; the staff went on to found PlatinumGames.
info.why: Panned by reviewers at launch and later reappraised as a cult classic. Clover's short catalogue gets collected as a set.

info.about: Michigan: Report from Hell is a video game developed by Grasshopper Manufacture. It was published in Japan by Spike in 2004, and in Europe by 505 GameStreet the following year.
info.trivia: You play entirely through a news camera. Point it at the wrong thing and your crew dies while you keep filming.
info.why: Never released in North America, so US collectors import the PAL disc, which was itself a small run.

info.about: Fatal Frame is a survival horror video game developed by Tecmo for PlayStation 2. The first entry in the Fatal Frame series, it was published by Tecmo in Japan (2001) and North America (2002), and by Wanadoo Edition in Europe in 2002.
info.trivia: Tecmo's camera-based horror game, marketed in the US as based on a true story.
info.why: Never re-released outside a Japanese PS3 download, so the disc is the only way to own it, and the series' following has grown.

info.about: Fatal Frame II: Crimson Butterfly is a survival horror video game developed by Tecmo for PlayStation 2. The second entry in the Fatal Frame series, it was published by Tecmo in 2003 in Japan and North America, and by Ubisoft in Europe in 2004.
info.trivia: Widely considered the peak of the series; the Wii remake never left Japan and Europe.
info.why: The most requested of the trilogy in the West and never re-released here, so it is consistently expensive.

info.about: Fatal Frame III: The Tormented is a survival horror video game developed by Tecmo for the PlayStation 2. The third entry in the Fatal Frame series, it was published by Tecmo in 2005 in Japan and North America, and by Take-Two Interactive in Europe in 2006.
info.trivia: The trilogy's finale, released in 2005 in the smallest numbers of the three.
info.why: The scarcest of the PS2 trilogy and never re-released physically, so it usually tops the series' prices.

info.about: Siren, known as Forbidden Siren in Europe and Australia, is a 2003 survival horror stealth video game developed and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: Sony Japan Studio's sightjacking horror game, from the director of the original Silent Hill.
info.why: A small North American print run for a punishingly hard game with a cult following; the PS3 Blood Curse is a remake, not this version.

info.about: Shadow of the Colossus is a 2005 action-adventure game developed and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It takes place in a fantasy setting and follows Wander, a young man who enters an isolated and abandoned region of the realm seeking the power to revive a girl named Mono.
info.trivia: There are no towns and no ordinary enemies. The entire game is sixteen boss fights and the ride between them.
info.why: Black label first pressings sit well above the Greatest Hits reprint that followed.

info.about: Ico is a 2001 action-adventure video game by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It was designed and directed by Fumito Ueda, who wanted to create a minimalist game based on a "boy meets girl" concept.
info.trivia: Fumito Ueda's design rule was subtraction: cut anything, including a HUD and music, that broke the feeling of two people alone.
info.why: The first US pressing sold poorly on release and is scarce, while the game's reputation grew steadily for two decades.

info.about: Ōkami is a 2006 action-adventure game developed by Clover Studio and published by Capcom. It was released for PlayStation 2 in 2006 in Japan and North America, and in 2007 in Europe and Australia.
info.trivia: The sumi-e ink art style was chosen partly because it hid the PS2's limited draw distance inside a deliberate aesthetic.
info.why: The original PS2 pressing predates every later port, and Clover's brief run of games is collected together.

info.about: Gitaroo Man is a rhythm video game developed by iNiS and published by Koei for PlayStation 2. It features visual production by Mitsuru Nakamura and an original soundtrack by Japanese band COIL.
info.trivia: Made by iNiS before the studio went on to Elite Beat Agents; the soundtrack was written first and the game built around it.
info.why: A small print run for an unusual rhythm game that never found a mainstream audience at retail.

info.about: Katamari Damacy is a 2004 action puzzle video game developed and published by Namco for the PlayStation 2. The game's plot concerns a diminutive prince on a mission to rebuild stars, constellations, and the Moon, which were inadvertently destroyed by his father, the King of All Cosmos.
info.trivia: Namco sold it for twenty dollars in the US, unusual for a new release.
info.why: Sold well at its budget price, and the REROLL remaster is everywhere, so the original stays affordable.

info.about: We Love Katamari is a 2005 action-puzzle video game developed and published by Namco for the PlayStation 2. It is the sequel and prequel to the 2004 sleeper hit Katamari Damacy.
info.trivia: The sequel made the fans within the game the reason for rolling.
info.why: Moderate supply; the 2023 remaster gives most players another route.

info.about: Persona 3, released outside Japan as Shin Megami Tensei: Persona 3, is a 2006 role-playing video game developed by Atlus. It is the fourth main installment in the Persona series, which is part of the larger Megami Tensei franchise.
info.trivia: FES added an epilogue campaign, The Answer, that is harder than the entire base game and has no social links.
info.why: The Atlus print run was modest and the series' audience multiplied years later.

info.about: Persona 4, released outside Japan as Shin Megami Tensei: Persona 4, is a 2008 role-playing video game by Atlus. It is chronologically the fifth installment in the Persona series, itself a part of the larger Megami Tensei franchise, and was released for the PlayStation 2 in Japan in July 2008, North America in December 2008, and in Europe and Australia in March 2009.
info.trivia: Released in late 2008, after the PS3 had been out for two years.
info.why: Popular and reprinted, but the Golden remake stayed on Vita and PC for years, so the PS2 disc has kept steady demand.

info.about: Shin Megami Tensei III: Nocturne is a role-playing video game developed by Atlus for the PlayStation 2. It was published by Atlus in Japan and North America, and by Ghostlight in Europe.
info.trivia: The first mainline SMT released in the West, with Dante from Devil May Cry as a guest.
info.why: The 2021 HD remaster covers players, but the first-print slipcover edition with the soundtrack remains a collector's target.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei: Digital Devil Saga

info.about: Shin Megami Tensei: Digital Devil Saga is a duology of role-playing video games developed by Atlus for the PlayStation 2. They are a spin-off of the Megami Tensei series.
info.trivia: An Atlus RPG where the party devours enemies to learn skills, the first half of a two-game story.
info.why: Never re-released, and the second half being scarcer drags interest in both games upward.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei: Digital Devil Saga 2

info.about: Shin Megami Tensei: Digital Devil Saga is a duology of role-playing video games developed by Atlus for the PlayStation 2. They are a spin-off of the Megami Tensei series.
info.trivia: The conclusion of the story, released months after the first in 2005.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than the first game and never re-released, so it is the more expensive of the pair.

games.title: Devil Summoner: Raidou Kuzunoha vs. The Soulless Army

info.about: Devil Summoner: Raidou Kuzunoha vs. the Soulless Army is a 2006 action role-playing game developed and published by Atlus for the PlayStation 2. The game is the third in the Devil Summoner series, which is a sub-series of the larger Megami Tensei franchise.
info.trivia: A 1930s Tokyo detective story from Atlus; a remaster arrived in 2025.
info.why: Never re-released until 2025, and the remaster brought new attention to the original disc.

info.about: Suikoden III is a role-playing video game developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 video game console, and the third installment in the Suikoden video game series.
info.trivia: The first 3D Suikoden, told from three perspectives; it never reached Europe.
info.why: A moderate print run, no European release and a devoted following keep it well above average.

info.about: Suikoden IV is a role-playing video game developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo and published by Konami exclusively for the PlayStation 2 video game console and is the fourth installment of the Suikoden video game series.
info.trivia: A seafaring prequel set 150 years before the first game.
info.why: The most common of the PS2 trilogy, so it prices below the others.

info.about: Suikoden V is a role-playing video game developed by Konami and Hudson Soft and published by Konami for the Sony PlayStation 2 video game console and the fifth and final main installment of the Suikoden video game series.
info.trivia: 108 recruitable characters, a series tradition, in the last mainline Suikoden Konami released.
info.why: Released at the end of the PS2's life to a shrinking JRPG retail audience, and the series stayed dormant for years afterwards.

info.about: Suikoden Tactics, originally released in Japan as Rhapsodia , is a tactical role-playing video game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 console as part of their Suikoden series. Initially released in Japan and North America in late 2005, the game was later made available in Europe and the PAL region in early 2006.
info.trivia: A tactical spin-off that continues Suikoden IV's story, released in 2005.
info.why: A small print run for a spin-off and no re-release make it the priciest PS2 Suikoden.

info.about: Xenosaga Episode I: Der Wille zur Macht is a role-playing video game developed by Monolith Soft and published by Namco for the PlayStation 2; the game was released in 2002 in Japan and 2003 in North America. It is the first entry in the Xenosaga trilogy and forms part of the wider Xeno metaseries.
info.trivia: Monolith Soft's space opera, famous for cutscenes that run for most of an hour.
info.why: The most common of the trilogy and never re-released, so it prices moderately.

info.about: Xenosaga Episode II: Jenseits von Gut und Böse is a 2004 role-playing video game developed by Monolith Soft for the PlayStation 2. It was published in Japan (2004) and North America (2005) by Namco, and in Europe by Sony Computer Entertainment Europe (2005).
info.trivia: The middle chapter, with redesigned characters and a divisive battle system.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than the first game after weaker reception, and never re-released.

info.about: Xenosaga Episode III: Also sprach Zarathustra is a role-playing video game developed by Monolith Soft and published by Namco Bandai Games for the PlayStation 2 in 2006. It is the final entry in both the Xenosaga trilogy and the larger Xenosaga series, which forms part of the Xeno franchise.
info.trivia: The trilogy was originally planned as six episodes; the story was compressed into three when the series was cut short.
info.why: The lowest print run of the three episodes, and completing the trilogy is what collectors are usually trying to do.

info.about: Shadow Hearts is a role-playing video game developed by Sacnoth for the PlayStation 2. Published in Japan by Aruze in 2001, it was published internationally by Midway Games in the same year and 2002 (Europe).
info.trivia: Released in the same week as Final Fantasy X, which buried it at retail.
info.why: A small Midway print run for a game overshadowed at launch, and no re-release since.

info.about: Shadow Hearts: Covenant is a role-playing video game developed by Nautilus (Sacnoth) for the PlayStation 2, and is the second entry in the Shadow Hearts series. Published in Japan by Aruze in 2004, the game was released internationally by Midway Games in 2004 and 2005 (Europe).
info.trivia: A two-disc sequel widely considered the series' best, published by Midway.
info.why: A modest print run and no re-release keep it climbing.

games.title: Shadow Hearts: From the New World

info.about: Shadow Hearts: From the New World is a role-playing video game developed by Nautilus (Sacnoth) for the PlayStation 2. It was published in Japan by Aruze in 2005, in North America by Xseed Games in 2006, and in Europe by Ghostlight in 2007.
info.trivia: It was XSEED's very first release, in 2006, before the publisher became known for Falcom and Marvelous titles.
info.why: A small debut print run from a new publisher, and the series has never returned.

info.about: Valkyrie Profile 2: Silmeria is the second installment of the Valkyrie Profile series, which was developed by tri-Ace and published by Square Enix. It was released for PlayStation 2 in 2006 in Japan and North America, and in 2007 in Australia and Europe.
info.trivia: A prequel set centuries before the first game, from tri-Ace.
info.why: Moderate supply and no re-release keep it mid-priced.

games.title: Star Ocean: Till the End of Time

info.about: Star Ocean: Till the End of Time is an action role-playing game, the third main game in the Star Ocean series. The game was developed by tri-Ace and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 2 console.
info.trivia: A two-disc RPG with a plot twist that recontextualises the whole series.
info.why: Common, and ported to PS4 in 2017, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Rogue Galaxy is an action role-playing video game developed by Level-5 and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: Level-5's space RPG, later ported to PS4.
info.why: Moderate supply and a PS4 version keep it mid-priced.

info.about: Dark Chronicle, released as Dark Cloud 2 in North America, is a 2002 action role-playing game developed by Level-5 and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2 (PS2). It was released in Japan before releasing in English in 2003.
info.trivia: Known as Dark Chronicle outside North America, with photography and invention systems.
info.why: Moderate supply; the PS4 port covers most players, so the disc is mid-priced.

info.about: Odin Sphere is an action role-playing game developed by Vanillaware for the PlayStation 2. It was published by Atlus in 2007, and by Square Enix in 2008.
info.trivia: Every frame is hand-drawn. Vanillaware's art pipeline was so labour-intensive that the studio nearly folded during production.
info.why: A late PS2 release from a studio with a devoted following, printed in modest numbers by Atlus.

info.about: GrimGrimoire is a 2007 real-time strategy video game developed by Vanillaware and published by Nippon Ichi Software and Koei (Europe) for the PlayStation 2. A remaster, GrimGrimoire OnceMore was released in Japan on PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch in 2022 and worldwide, along with a PlayStation 5 version, in 2023.
info.trivia: Vanillaware's real-time strategy game, remastered as OnceMore in 2023.
info.why: A small print run for a niche genre on PS2, and the remaster renewed attention.

info.about: Disgaea: Hour of Darkness is a tactical role-playing video game developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: Damage numbers run into the millions and the level cap is 9999, which was the joke and the point.
info.why: The first Atlus pressing was small; the series only became reliably popular from the sequels onwards.

info.about: Disgaea 2: Cursed Memories is a tactical role-playing game developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software for the PlayStation 2 video game console. Disgaea 2 is the sequel to 2003's Disgaea: Hour of Darkness and was released for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: The sequel to Hour of Darkness, later ported to PSP and PC.
info.why: Moderate supply and several other versions keep it mid-priced.

info.about: Phantom Brave is a tactical role-playing game for the PlayStation 2 video game console, developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software. It was released on January 22, 2004 in Japan, on August 31, 2004 in North America and on February 4, 2005 in Europe.
info.trivia: Nippon Ichi's grid-free tactics game, ported to Wii, PSP and PC.
info.why: Moderate supply and many ports keep the PS2 disc mid-priced.

info.about: La Pucelle: Tactics is a tactical role-playing game developed by Nippon Ichi Software for the PlayStation 2. It was released in Japan in January 2002, and in North America by Mastiff in May 2004.
info.trivia: Nippon Ichi's first tactics game, published in the West by Mastiff.
info.why: A small print run from a minor publisher and no re-release keep it scarce.

games.title: Makai Kingdom: Chronicles of the Sacred Tome

info.about: Makai Kingdom: Chronicles of the Sacred Tome is a tactical role-playing game developed and published by Nippon Ichi Software. It was initially released for PlayStation 2 on March 17, 2005 in Japan, July 26 in North America, and October 28 in Europe.
info.trivia: A Nippon Ichi tactics game with free movement, remastered in 2021.
info.why: A moderate print run; the remaster covers players but not the disc.

info.about: Ar tonelico: Melody of Elemia, released in Japan as Ar tonelico: The Girl Who Keeps Singing at the End of the World is a role-playing video game developed by Gust Corporation for the PlayStation 2 and originally published by Banpresto in 2006.
info.trivia: A Gust RPG built around song magic, published by NIS America in 2007.
info.why: A small print run and no re-release; the series never left PlayStation.

games.title: Ar tonelico II: Melody of Metafalica

info.about: Ar tonelico II: Melody of Metafalica, known in Japan as Ar tonelico II: Sekai ni Hibiku Shōjo-tachi no Metafalica is a role-playing video game, developed by Gust for the PlayStation 2 which was released in Japan on October 25, 2007, in North America on January 20, 2009, and was set to be released in the EU on 29 May 2009, but a problem with the barcode delayed it by a week.
info.trivia: The North American release in 2009 shipped with a bug that could crash the final boss fight.
info.why: A very late, small print run for a niche RPG, and no re-release, make it one of the priciest NIS America PS2 titles.

info.about: Mana Khemia: Alchemists of Al-Revis is a role-playing video game developed by Gust Co. Ltd. in 2007 for the PlayStation 2. The game is the ninth entry to Gust's Atelier series and incorporates elements of standard turn-based combat and alchemy.
info.trivia: A Gust RPG set in an alchemy academy, later ported to PSP as Student Alliance.
info.why: A small print run and no re-release of this version keep it scarce.

info.about: Steambot Chronicles is a 2005 action role-playing game developed and published by Irem Software Engineering in Japan for the PlayStation 2, set during an alternate universe Industrial Revolution where machines called 'Trotmobiles' became the standard for modern transportation and industrial machinery.
info.trivia: Irem's open-ended adventure with mechs, harmonica busking and a band to join, published by Atlus in 2006.
info.why: A small Atlus print run for a cult title that was never re-released.

info.about: A two-disc set bringing Growlanser II and Growlanser III to North America in 2004, and the final release from Working Designs.
info.trivia: Working Designs' final release before the publisher closed in 2005, bundling Growlanser II and III with a deluxe edition.
info.why: A small print run from a publisher that no longer exists, with a collector following for everything Working Designs made.

info.about: Growlanser: Heritage of War is a tactical role-playing video game for the PlayStation 2. It was developed by Career Soft, and published in Japan by Atlus in 2006.
info.trivia: Atlus brought the fifth Growlanser to the US in 2007.
info.why: A small late-life print run and no re-release.

info.about: Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater is a 2004 action-adventure stealth game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2. It was released in late 2004 in North America and Japan, and in early 2005 in Europe and Australia.
info.trivia: A three-disc re-release adding a movable camera, online play and the original MSX Metal Gear games.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than Snake Eater and preferred for its camera and the MSX games, so it prices well above the original.

games.title: Zone of the Enders: The 2nd Runner

info.about: Zone of the Enders: The 2nd Runner, known in Japan as Anubis: Zone of the Enders, is an action hack and slash video game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 in 2003. The sequel to Zone of the Enders is based around mecha combat with the player once again controlling the "Orbital Frame" Jehuty.
info.trivia: Kojima Productions' mech game with a hand-drawn art style, remastered twice since.
info.why: Moderate supply; the HD and Mars remasters give players other routes, so the disc is mid-priced.

info.about: Devil May Cry 3: Dante's Awakening is a 2005 action-adventure game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. The game is a prequel to the original Devil May Cry, featuring a younger Dante.
info.trivia: A revised release adding a playable Vergil and an easier difficulty for the West.
info.why: Sold as a Greatest Hits title in large numbers, so prices are moderate.

info.about: Resident Evil Outbreak is a survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. It was released on December 11, 2003 in Japan, on March 30, 2004 in North America, and on September 17, 2004 in PAL regions.
info.trivia: The first online Resident Evil; the US servers closed in 2007.
info.why: Common enough, but with online play gone and no re-release, the disc is the only way to own it.

info.about: Resident Evil Outbreak: File #2 is a survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom with online playability for the PlayStation 2. It is the sequel to Resident Evil Outbreak, and the final installment of the spin-off series.
info.trivia: A second set of scenarios released in 2005, again with online play that has since closed.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than the first Outbreak and never re-released, so it prices above it.

info.about: Gradius V is a 2004 scrolling shooter video game published by Konami for the PlayStation 2. It was largely developed under contract by Treasure, who had previously worked on Radiant Silvergun and Ikaruga.
info.trivia: Treasure developed this entry for Konami, with a soundtrack by Hitoshi Sakimoto.
info.why: A small print run for a shooter and no Western re-release keep it among the pricier PS2 shooters.

info.about: R-Type Final is a horizontal shooter video game by Irem for the PlayStation 2 video game console. It was planned to be the last mainline game in the R-Type series.
info.trivia: Irem's farewell to the series, with more than a hundred unlockable ships.
info.why: A modest print run for a shooter; the 2021 sequel renewed interest without replacing it.

info.about: Raiden III is a vertically scrolling shooter developed by MOSS and released in as an arcade video game in 2005. It is the fourth game in Seibu Kaihatsu's Raiden series; it is the first installment in the series to be developed by MOSS as it consists of former Seibu Kaihatsu employees who bought the rights to the series.
info.trivia: UFO Interactive brought the arcade shooter to the US in 2007.
info.why: A tiny late-life print run from a minor publisher makes it one of the scarcest PS2 shooters.

info.about: Castlevania: Lament of Innocence is a 2003 action-adventure game developed by Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 console. Part of Konami's Castlevania video game series, it is the first installment of the series on the PlayStation 2 and the third to make use of a 3D style of gameplay.
info.trivia: The series' first 3D entry that was well received, set at the origin of the Belmont curse.
info.why: Moderate supply and no re-release keep it mid-priced.

info.about: Castlevania: Curse of Darkness is a 2005 action role-playing game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox. It is the fourth 3D title in the Castlevania series, following Castlevania: Lament of Innocence (2003).
info.trivia: A sequel to Castlevania III with a companion-raising system.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than Lament of Innocence and never re-released, so it prices above it.

info.about: Contra: Shattered Soldier is a video game that is part of the Contra series by Konami. It was developed by Team Kijirushi, a group of staff members within Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo.
info.trivia: Konami's return to 2D Contra after two panned PlayStation entries.
info.why: A modest print run for a hard, niche game and no re-release keep it climbing.

info.about: Marvel vs. Capcom 2: New Age of Heroes is a 2000 crossover fighting game developed and published by Capcom for arcades. It is the fourth installment in the Marvel vs. Capcom series, which features characters from both Capcom's video game franchises and comic book series published by Marvel Comics.
info.trivia: Capcom's Marvel licence lapsed, and the game vanished from stores for over a decade until the 2024 collection.
info.why: A generation of players who could not buy it anywhere kept demand for the disc high; the 2024 re-release eased it only slightly.

info.about: Capcom vs. SNK 2: Mark of the Millennium 2001 is a 2001 crossover fighting game developed and published by Capcom. The sequel to Capcom vs. SNK: Millennium Fight 2000 (2000) and an entry in the SNK vs. Capcom series, it was originally released on NAOMI hardware in arcades, with Sega handling the North American arcade release.
info.trivia: The PS2 version added extra grooves and is the basis of the competitive scene's preferred build.
info.why: Moderate supply, but sustained tournament interest and a long gap without re-release keep it expensive.

info.about: Guilty Gear X2, also known as Guilty Gear XX and subtitled The Midnight Carnival in Japan, is a fighting game developed by Arc System Works and published by Sammy Studios. The third main installment of the Guilty Gear series, Guilty Gear X2 furthered the plot of the series, as well as introduced new characters and gameplay mechanics.
info.trivia: A revision released in 2007, later superseded by Plus and Plus R on other platforms.
info.why: A late, small print run of one specific revision, so it is scarcer than the game itself.

info.about: The Warriors is a 2005 beat 'em up video game developed by Rockstar Toronto and published by Rockstar Games. Based on the 1979 film of the same name; it was released in October 2005 for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox, and February 2007 for the PlayStation Portable; the PSP port was developed by Rockstar Leeds.
info.trivia: Rockstar's adaptation of the 1979 film, with the original cast returning to voice their characters.
info.why: A moderate print run; the licence makes re-release complicated, and a PS4 download came only in 2016.

info.about: Bully is a 2006 action-adventure video game developed by Rockstar Vancouver and published by Rockstar Games. Set in the fictional New England town of Bullworth, the game follows juvenile delinquent student Jimmy Hopkins, who is involuntarily enrolled at Bullworth Academy, the town's prestigious boarding school.
info.trivia: Rockstar Vancouver's school-set open world, briefly the subject of a lawsuit before release.
info.why: The game was reprinted as a Greatest Hits title, so original black-label copies carry the premium; the Scholarship Edition ports keep the game itself available.

info.about: Def Jam: Fight for NY is a 3D fighting video game developed by AKI Corporation and EA Canada and published by EA Games. It was released for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and Xbox on September 21, 2004.
info.trivia: A wrestling game whose roster is licensed rappers, from Method Man to Snoop Dogg.
info.why: Dozens of licensed artists and tracks make a re-release practically impossible, and a cult following keeps demand high.

info.about: Killer7 is a 2005 action-adventure game developed by Grasshopper Manufacture and Capcom and published by Capcom for the GameCube and PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: Suda51's cel-shaded assassin game, one of the Capcom Five, ported to PS2 with censorship changes.
info.why: Moderate supply; a PC port in 2018 covers players, so prices are mid-range.

info.about: Gungrave is a 2002 Japanese third-person shooter video game developed and published by Red Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.
info.trivia: Red Entertainment's shooter with character designs by Yasuhiro Nightow of Trigun.
info.why: Moderate supply and no re-release; the 2022 sequel renewed some interest.

info.about: Gungrave: Overdose is a PlayStation 2 third-person shooter video game developed by animation studio Ikusabune and published by Red Entertainment in Japan and by Mastiff in North America, and a direct sequel to Gungrave. The game was released on March 4, 2004, in Japan, September 15, 2004, in North America and October 7, 2005, in the PAL regions.
info.trivia: A budget-priced sequel that sold for twenty dollars at launch.
info.why: Printed in smaller numbers than the first game and never re-released, so it prices above it.

games.title: Blood Will Tell: Tezuka Osamu's Dororo

info.about: Blood Will Tell: Tezuka Osamu's Dororo, released as Dororo (どろろ) in Japan, is a 2004 PlayStation 2 game released by Sega. It is based on the Japanese manga series Dororo, which was created by Osamu Tezuka.
info.trivia: Sega's adaptation of Osamu Tezuka's manga Dororo, in which the hero reclaims his stolen body parts.
info.why: A small US print run for an oddity that was never re-released, so it is one of the scarcer Sega PS2 titles.

info.about: Chulip (チュウリップ), stylized as Chu♥lip, is an adventure/simulation video game developed by Punchline and released on October 3, 2002, in Japan by Victor Interactive Software for the PlayStation 2. After numerous delays, the game was released in North America by Natsume Inc. on February 13, 2007, as a GameStop-exclusive title.
info.trivia: A game about kissing everyone in town, published in the US by Natsume in 2007.
info.why: A tiny late-life print run for a cult title; among the rarest US PS2 discs.

info.about: Way of the Samurai 2 is a PlayStation 2 (PS2) action-adventure game released in 2003.
info.trivia: Acquire's open-ended samurai sandbox, published in the US by Capcom.
info.why: A modest print run and no re-release keep it above average.

info.about: Front Mission 4, also known in Japan as Front Mission Fourth, is a tactical role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 2. It is the fourth main installment of the Front Mission series.
info.trivia: The only PS2 Front Mission released in the West.
info.why: Moderate supply and no remake, unlike earlier entries, keep it steady.

info.about: Ring of Red is an alternate history turn-based strategy video game released by Konami for the PlayStation 2 console. It was one of the first PlayStation 2 games made with CD-ROM-based technology.
info.trivia: Konami's alternate-history mech tactics game, an early PS2 release.
info.why: A small print run for a niche strategy game and no re-release.

info.about: Klonoa 2: Lunatea's Veil is a 2001 platform game developed and published by Namco for the PlayStation 2. It is the third installment in the Klonoa series and a sequel to Klonoa: Moonlight Museum (1999).
info.trivia: Namco's 2.5D platformer, unreissued until the 2022 Phantasy Reverie collection.
info.why: A modest print run and twenty years without a re-release keep the disc pricey even after the collection.

info.about: TimeSplitters: Future Perfect is a 2005 first-person shooter video game developed by Free Radical Design and published by Electronic Arts for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, and Xbox.
info.trivia: Free Radical's third and last TimeSplitters, with a map maker and time-travelling co-op.
info.why: The studio's collapse means no re-release, and it is the series' most requested entry.

info.about: Dragon Quest VIII: Journey of the Cursed King is a 2004 role-playing video game developed by Level-5 and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 2. It was first released in Japan in November 2004, followed by North America in November 2005 and PAL regions in April 2006.
info.trivia: The first-run black-label release, which shipped with a Final Fantasy XII demo disc.
info.why: The game is common, so the premium is for the black label with the demo disc over the Greatest Hits reprint.

info.about: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is a 2004 action-adventure game developed by Rockstar North and published by Rockstar Games. It is the fifth main game in the Grand Theft Auto series and the seventh overall entry, following 2002's Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a 2002 action-adventure game developed by Rockstar North and published by Rockstar Games. It is the fourth main game in the Grand Theft Auto series, following 2001's Grand Theft Auto III, and the sixth entry overall.
Grand Theft Auto III is a 2001 action-adventure game developed by DMA Design and published by Rockstar Games. It is the first 3D game in the Grand Theft Auto series.

Kingdom Hearts is a 2002 action role-playing game developed and published by Square for the PlayStation 2. It is the first game in the Kingdom Hearts series and is the result of a collaboration between Square and The Walt Disney Company.

Kingdom Hearts II is a 2005 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix in collaboration with Buena Vista Games for the PlayStation 2. The game is a sequel to Kingdom Hearts, and like the original game, combines characters and settings from Disney films with those of Square Enix's Final Fantasy series.

Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories is a 2004 action role-playing game developed by Square Enix and Jupiter and published by Square Enix in collaboration with Disney Interactive for the Game Boy Advance (GBA). The second game in the Kingdom Hearts series, it is a direct sequel to Kingdom Hearts whose ending is set about a year before the events of Kingdom Hearts II.

Final Fantasy X is a 2001 role-playing video game developed and published by Square for PlayStation 2. The tenth main installment in the Final Fantasy series, it is the first game in the series to feature fully three-dimensional areas, and voice acting.

Final Fantasy X-2 is a 2003 role-playing video game developed and published by Square for the PlayStation 2. Unlike most Final Fantasy games, which use self-contained stories and characters, X-2 continues the story of Final Fantasy X (2001).
Final Fantasy XII is a 2006 role-playing video game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 2 in March 2006.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty

info.about: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty is a 2001 action-adventure stealth game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2. Directed, produced, designed, and written by Hideo Kojima, it is the fourth mainline game in the Metal Gear series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to Metal Gear Solid (1998).

Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater is a 2004 action-adventure stealth game developed and published by Konami for the PlayStation 2. It was released in late 2004 in North America and Japan, and in early 2005 in Europe and Australia.
Resident Evil 4 is a 2005 survival horror game developed and published by Capcom for the GameCube. Players control the special agent Leon S.

Resident Evil – Code: Veronica is a 2000 survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom for the Dreamcast. It was the first Resident Evil game to debut on a platform other than PlayStation.

Devil May Cry is a 2001 action-adventure game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. Set on a remote island, the story centers on Dante, a demon hunter who uses his business to carry out a lifelong vendetta against all demons.

God of War is a 2005 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE). First released for the PlayStation 2 on March 22, 2005, the game is the first installment in the God of War series and the fourth chronologically.

God of War II is a 2007 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE). First released for the PlayStation 2 on March 13, 2007, the game is the second installment in the God of War series, the seventh chronologically, and the sequel to 2005's God of War.

games.title: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy

info.about: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy is a 2001 platform video game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2 (PS2). The player controls Jak, who sets out to reverse the transformation of his friend Daxter into an "ottsel", a fictional hybrid of an otter and a weasel.

Jak II is a 2003 platform video game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2 (PS2). A sequel to Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy (2001), it places the protagonist Jak in the dystopian Haven City, where he pursues vengeance against the tyrannical Baron Praxis after two years of torturous experiments.

Jak 3 is a 2004 action-adventure platformer video game developed by Naughty Dog and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2 (PS2). The game is the sequel to Jak II (2003) and serves as the conclusion of the trilogy.

Ratchet & Clank is a 2002 third-person shooter platform video game developed by Insomniac Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2 in 2002. It is the first installment in the Ratchet & Clank series as well as the first game developed by Insomniac to not be owned by Universal Interactive.

Ratchet & Clank: Going Commando is a 2003 third-person shooter platform video game developed by Insomniac Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the second game in the Ratchet & Clank series, following Ratchet & Clank (2002).
Ratchet & Clank: Up Your Arsenal is a 2004 third-person shooter platform video game developed by Insomniac Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.

Ratchet: Deadlocked is a 2005 third-person shooter platform video game developed by Insomniac Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the fourth installment of the Ratchet & Clank series.

games.title: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus

info.about: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus is a 2002 stealth platform video game developed by Sucker Punch Productions and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the first installment in the Sly Cooper series.
Sly 2: Band of Thieves is a 2004 stealth action video game developed by Sucker Punch Productions and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.
Sly 3: Honor Among Thieves is a 2005 stealth action video game developed by Sucker Punch Productions and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.

Dark Cloud is an 2000 action role-playing game developed by Level-5 and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. Originally intended as a launch title for the system, the game was eventually released in Japan in December 2000, in North America in May 2001, and in Europe in September 2001.

Gran Turismo 3: A-Spec is a 2001 sim racing video game developed by Polyphony Digital and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the third installment in the Gran Turismo series.

Gran Turismo 4 is a 2004 sim racing video game developed by Polyphony Digital and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the fourth main installment and the sixth overall in the Gran Turismo series.

Tekken 5 (鉄拳5) is a 2004 fighting game developed and published by Namco for arcades, before being ported to the PlayStation 2 in 2005. It is the fifth main game in the Tekken series, marking the tenth anniversary of the series.
Tekken Tag Tournament is a 1999 fighting game developed and published by Namco for arcades. It is a spin-off the Tekken series.

Soulcalibur III is a 2005 fighting game developed and published by Namco as a sequel to Soulcalibur II (2002) and the fourth installment in the Soulcalibur series. It was originally released for the PlayStation 2 and was followed by an improved arcade version, subtitled Arcade Edition, in 2006.
Virtua Fighter 4 is a 2001 fighting video game developed by Sega AM2 and published by Sega for arcades. It is the fourth game installment in the Virtua Fighter series.

Burnout 3: Takedown is a 2004 racing video game developed by Criterion Games and published by Electronic Arts. It is the third instalment in the Burnout series, which is characterised by fast-paced arcade racing.

Need for Speed: Most Wanted is a 2005 racing video game, and the ninth installment in the Need for Speed series following Underground 2. Developed and published by Electronic Arts (EA), it was released in November 2005 for GameCube, PlayStation 2, Windows, Xbox, and Xbox 360 alongside two distinct versions for Nintendo DS and Game Boy Advance.
SSX 3 is a 2003 snowboarding video game developed by EA Canada and published by Electronic Arts under the EA Sports BIG label.

SSX Tricky, also known as SSX 2 or SSX 2: Tricky, is a snowboarding video game, the second game in the SSX series published by Electronic Arts under the EA Sports BIG label and developed by EA Canada. A direct sequel to SSX, the game was originally released in 2001 for PlayStation 2, GameCube, and Xbox, and was later ported to the Game Boy Advance in 2002.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3 is a 2001 skateboarding video game and the third installment in the Tony Hawk's series. It was published by Activision under the Activision O2 label in 2001 for the PlayStation, PlayStation 2, Game Boy Color and GameCube.

Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4 is a 2002 skateboarding game developed by Neversoft and published by Activision under their Activision O2 label. The game was ported by different developers to various systems.

Tony Hawk's Underground is a 2003 skateboarding video game and the fifth entry in the Tony Hawk's series, following Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4. It was developed by Neversoft and published by Activision for the GameCube, PlayStation 2, Xbox, and Game Boy Advance.

Star Wars: Battlefront is a 2004 first and third-person shooter video game based on the Star Wars film franchise. Developed by Pandemic Studios and published by LucasArts, it is the first installment in the Star Wars: Battlefront series.

Star Wars: Battlefront II is a 2005 first and third-person shooter video game based on the Star Wars film franchise. Developed by Pandemic Studios and published by LucasArts, it is a sequel to 2004's Star Wars: Battlefront and the second installment in the Star Wars: Battlefront series.

Ace Combat 04: Shattered Skies is a 2001 combat flight simulation video game developed and published by Namco for the PlayStation 2. It is the fourth entry in the Ace Combat series and the first to be released for the PlayStation 2.
Ace Combat 5: The Unsung War is a 2004 combat flight simulation game by Namco for the PlayStation 2. It is the fifth installment of the Ace Combat series.

games.title: Ace Combat Zero: The Belkan War

info.about: Ace Combat Zero: The Belkan War is a 2006 combat flight simulation video game developed and published by Namco for the PlayStation 2. Part of the Ace Combat series, the Japanese version of the game was the last title to be released by Namco, and the North American version being the first game to be released by the newly formed Namco Bandai Games.
Onimusha: Warlords, known in Japan as Onimusha , is a 2001 action-adventure game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. It is the first entry of the Onimusha series.

Onimusha 2: Samurai's Destiny, released in Japan as Onimusha 2 , is a 2002 action-adventure game developed and released by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. It is the second installment in the Onimusha series and was released in March 2002.

Onimusha 3: Demon Siege, released in Japan and Europe as Onimusha 3 , is a 2004 action-adventure game developed and published by Capcom. It is the third game of the Onimusha series and was released for the PlayStation 2 in April 2004, and later ported to Windows in December 2005.

Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams, released in Japan as Shin Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams , is a 2006 action role-playing game developed and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. It is the sixth installment of Capcom's Onimusha series, and the fourth game in the canonical main series.

Maximo: Ghosts to Glory, known in Japan, Korea, Europe and Australia as Maximo , is a 3D hack and slash platform video game developed by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. The game is based on the Ghosts 'n Goblins universe and features original character designs by Japanese manga artist Susumu Matsushita.

Maximo vs. Army of Zin is an action-adventure game developed and published by Capcom and developed by their US-based Production Studio 8 in 2003 for the PlayStation 2 video game console. It is a sequel to Maximo: Ghosts to Glory and part of the Ghosts 'n Goblins franchise.

Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 3, released as Dragon Ball Z3 in Japan, is a video game based on the popular anime series Dragon Ball Z and was developed by Dimps for the PlayStation 2. The game was published by Atari in North America and Australia, and Bandai in Europe and Japan.
Yakuza is a 2005 action-adventure game developed and published by Sega for the PlayStation 2. It was released in December 2005 in Japan and in September 2006 internationally.
Yakuza 2 is a 2006 action-adventure game developed and published by Sega for the PlayStation 2.
Tales of the Abyss is an action role-playing game developed by Namco Tales Studio. It is the eighth main title in their Tales series and was released in celebration of the series' 10th anniversary.
Tales of Legendia is an action role-playing game that was developed and published by Namco for the PlayStation 2. It is the seventh mainline title in their Tales series.

Wild Arms 3, known in Japan as Wild Arms Advanced 3rd, is a role-playing video game developed by Media.Vision and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is a sequel to Wild Arms and Wild Arms 2.

Wild Arms 4, known in Japan as Wild Arms the 4th Detonator, is a role-playing video game developed by Media.Vision and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the fourth installment in the Wild Arms video game series.

Wild Arms 5, released in Japan as Wild Arms: The Fifth Vanguard, is a turn-based role-playing video game developed by Media.Vision and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the fifth main instalment of the Wild Arms series.

Wild Arms is a role-playing video game developed by Media.Vision and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation. The game was released in Japan in 1996, in North America in 1997, and in Europe in 1998.

Grandia III is a role-playing video game developed by Game Arts and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 2 console. Originally released in Japan in August 2005, the game was released in English in North America in February 2006, and is the first main series Grandia title to not be released in Europe.
Grandia Xtreme is a role-playing video game developed by Game Arts and published by Enix for the PlayStation 2 video game console in January 2002. The game is part of the Grandia series.
Breath of Fire: Dragon Quarter is a 2002 role-playing game by Capcom for the PlayStation 2.

MagnaCarta: Tears of Blood simply known as MagnaCarta is a role-playing video game developed by Softmax and published by Banpresto for the PlayStation 2 in Japan, Atlus in North America, and 505 Game Street in PAL regions. Sony Computer Entertainment released the game in Softmax's native country South Korea as MagnaCarta: Crimson Stigmata .
Radiata Stories is an action role-playing video game developed by tri-Ace and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation 2.
Okage: Shadow King, known in Japan as Boku to Maō, is a 2001 role-playing video game developed by Zener Works and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.
Shinobi is a 2002 action-adventure game developed by Overworks and published by Sega for the PlayStation 2. It is part of the Shinobi series.

Manhunt is a 2003 stealth game developed by Rockstar North and published by Rockstar Games. It was released for the PlayStation 2 in November 2003, followed by Microsoft Windows and Xbox releases in April 2004.

Red Dead Revolver is a 2004 action-adventure game developed by Rockstar San Diego and published by Rockstar Games. It is the first entry in the Red Dead series, and was released for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox in May 2004.

Killzone is a 2004 first-person shooter video game developed by Guerrilla Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It is the first installment of the Killzone series and the first partnership between Guerrilla and Sony.

Twisted Metal: Black is a 2001 vehicular combat game developed by Incog Inc. Entertainment and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. The fifth title of the Twisted Metal series following Twisted Metal 4 (1999), it serves as a reboot of the franchise.
Midnight Club 3: Dub Edition is a 2005 racing video game developed by Rockstar San Diego and published by Rockstar Games. It is the third installment in the Midnight Club series.

Mortal Kombat: Deception is a 2004 fighting game developed and published by Midway. The sixth main installment in the Mortal Kombat franchise and sequel to Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance (2002), it was released for the PlayStation 2 (PS2) and Xbox in October 2004, the GameCube in March 2005, and for the PlayStation Portable (PSP) as Mortal Kombat: Unchained in November 2006.

Mortal Kombat: Armageddon is a 2006 fighting game developed and published by Midway for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox, with a later port for the Wii developed by Just Games Interactive. It is the seventh main installment in the Mortal Kombat franchise, and a sequel to 2004's Mortal Kombat: Deception.

Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks is a 2005 action-adventure game developed and published by Midway for the PlayStation 2 and Xbox. A spin-off of the Mortal Kombat franchise, it is a retelling of the events of Mortal Kombat II (1993).
Spider-Man 2 is a 2004 action-adventure game based on the 2004 film of the same name. The game is the sequel to 2002's Spider-Man, itself based on the 2002 film of the same name.
The Simpsons: Hit & Run is a 2003 action-adventure game developed by Radical Entertainment and published by Vivendi Universal Games.

games.title: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time

info.about: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time is a 2003 action-adventure game developed by Ubisoft Montreal and published by Ubisoft. The game was released on the Game Boy Advance, PlayStation 2, GameCube, Xbox and Windows in November 2003.

games.title: Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex

info.about: Crash Bandicoot: The Wrath of Cortex is a 2001 platform game developed by Traveller's Tales and published by Universal Interactive for the PlayStation 2, Xbox, and GameCube. It was first released for the PlayStation 2 in late 2001, and for the Xbox in April 2002; it was later ported to the GameCube by Eurocom Entertainment Software and was released in late 2002.

Champions of Norrath: Realms of EverQuest is a 2004 action role-playing video game for the PlayStation 2, set in the EverQuest universe. The game is playable with one single player or cooperative for up to four players, but with a Network Adapter, players can take the game online with others and kill others or join to form groups of adventurers.

Champions: Return to Arms is a 2005 action role-playing video game developed by Snowblind Studios and published by Sony Online Entertainment for the PlayStation 2 Set in the EverQuest universe, it is the sequel to Champions of Norrath.

Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance is a 2001 action role-playing video game developed by Snowblind Studios and published by Interplay Entertainment subsidiary Black Isle Studios for the PlayStation 2 and the Xbox consoles, with High Voltage Software handling the GameCube port and Magic Pockets developing the Game Boy Advance version.

Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance II is a 2004 hack and slash action role-playing game for PlayStation 2 and Xbox developed by Black Isle Studios and published by Interplay Entertainment, with distribution handled by Vivendi Universal Games in North America and Avalon Interactive/Acclaim Entertainment in Europe.

games.title: X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse

info.about: X-Men Legends II: Rise of Apocalypse is an action role-playing game developed by Raven Software and published by Activision. It is the follow-up to 2004's X-Men Legends.

Marvel: Ultimate Alliance is a 2006 action role-playing game developed by Raven Software and published by Activision. Ultimate Alliance is set within the fictional Marvel Universe and features many of the superheroes, supervillains, and supporting characters that appear in publications by Marvel Comics.

Def Jam Vendetta is a 3D professional wrestling fighting video game developed by AKI Corporation and EA Canada and published by Electronic Arts under the EA Sports BIG label. It was released for the GameCube and PlayStation 2 in April 2003.

NBA Street Vol. 2 is a basketball video game developed by NuFX and EA Canada and published by Electronic Arts under the EA Sports BIG label. It is the sequel to NBA Street and the second installment in the NBA Street series.

Rez is a music rail shooter video game developed by United Game Artists and published by Sega for the Dreamcast and PlayStation 2. It was released in Japan in 2001, followed by releases to the United States and Europe in 2002.
Amplitude is a 2003 rhythm video game developed by Harmonix and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.

Sky Odyssey, known in Japan as The Sky Odyssey , is a flight simulation video game developed by Cross, XAX Entertainment and Future Creates and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It was released in 2000 in North America by Activision and 2001 internationally.

Clock Tower 3 is a survival horror video game co-produced by Capcom and Sunsoft for the PlayStation 2. Released in 2002, it is the fourth installment in the Clock Tower series, and the only video game directed by Japanese film director Kinji Fukasaku.

Echo Night: Beyond, known in Japan as Nebula: Echo Night, is a 2004 survival horror adventure video game developed by FromSoftware for the PlayStation 2 console. Agetec published the game in North America, with the European release, by Indie Games, following in August 2005.

Ape Escape 2 is a 2002 platform game developed and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2. It was released in Japan in July 2002, Europe in March 2003 and North America in July 2003 by Ubi Soft.
Ape Escape 3 is a 2005 platform game developed and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 2.
TimeSplitters 2 is a first-person shooter video game, developed by Free Radical Design, published by Eidos Interactive, and released in October 2002 for PlayStation 2, Xbox and GameCube.

Zone of the Enders , officially abbreviated as Z.O.E., is a 2001 action hack-and-slash video game developed and published by Konami for the Sony PlayStation 2. The game is based around mecha combat in outer space.
Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII is a 2007 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix for the PlayStation Portable.
info.trivia: The combat runs on a slot machine that fires abilities and cutscenes at random while you fight.
info.why: The original UMD predates the Reunion remaster, and sealed copies are chased by Final Fantasy VII collectors.

info.about: Persona 3, released outside Japan as Shin Megami Tensei: Persona 3, is a 2006 role-playing video game developed by Atlus. It is the fourth main installment in the Persona series, which is part of the larger Megami Tensei franchise.
info.trivia: It added a female protagonist and remains the only version with that route until the 2023 remaster.
info.why: Popular and reprinted, so the UMD is affordable; the remaster gives most players a digital route.

info.about: Persona 2: Innocent Sin is a 1999 role-playing video game developed and published by Atlus for the PlayStation. It is the second entry in the Persona series, itself a subseries of the Megami Tensei franchise, and acts as a sequel to the original Persona.
info.trivia: The first time Innocent Sin was released outside Japan, in September 2011 near the end of the PSP's life.
info.why: Atlus printed very few copies that late, and it has never been re-released, so it is one of the most expensive PSP games.

games.title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together
